methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Ark Electronics is a private-stage company operating in Robotics & Manufacturing, where comparable valuation anchors are sparse and dispersed. The addressable peer universe comprises 1 public company (ticker 277810.KQ) and 8 private peers, including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics. However, the narrow peer-median method is inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier matches within the sector—the analysis identified 11 same-sector peers overall but zero qualifying datapoints under tight stage and valuation-tier filters, the threshold for reliable median derivation being 3 or more.

Given this constraint, traditional triangulation proves limited. The sparse public comparables and heterogeneous private peer cohort preclude confident median-based benchmarking. Any valuation range derived from this dataset would rest heavily on sector-wide multiples applied to undisclosed financial metrics, introducing material estimation error.

A credible valuation narrative for Ark Electronics therefore requires either: (1) disclosure of revenue, EBITDA, or growth rates to anchor relative-value methods; (2) expansion of comparable set to adjacent subsectors (automation, industrial software) to improve datapoint density; or (3) reliance on forward venture-method assumptions tied to deployment capital and exit multiples. Without additional financial detail, quantitative range-setting is not warranted.
